# shop-front

## Project overview

Storefront for a small bakery.

## Language policy

- Code, comments, docs and commit messages: English.
- Replies to the user: English.

## Tech stack

Uses: TypeScript, Node.js, npm.

- Use the Node.js version pinned in `.nvmrc` or in the `engines` field of package.json, never whatever version is installed globally. Why: Node.js versions differ in behavior and break native dependencies.
- Use npm for every install and script, and commit package-lock.json. Never run pnpm or yarn. Why: Mixing package managers creates conflicting lockfiles.

## Code style

- Keep `strict` enabled in tsconfig.json. Never use `any`; use `unknown` and narrow it. Why: Strict types catch errors at compile time, and `any` silently turns the checks off.

## Agent workflow

- Never edit the agent instruction files or `cyanotype.yaml` yourself. When you learn a convention, or are corrected twice on the same point, propose a rule with its reason for the user to approve. Why: The instruction files are generated from `cyanotype.yaml`, so direct edits are lost and unreviewed rules creep in.

## Safety rules

- Keep secrets in `.env`, which stays in `.gitignore`; never hardcode or commit them, and do not read `.env` files. When you add a variable, add its name with a placeholder value to `.env.example`. Why: A committed secret stays in git history and has to be rotated.

## Claude Code

- Deny rules in .claude/settings.json back the safety rules; when one blocks an action, stop and ask instead of reaching the same result another way.
